name: polygon-angles
title: Polygon angles
tagline: Single polygon with interior and/or exterior angles marked and the angle sum derived; regular or irregular, triangle-split, with algebraic-label questions.
description: A single polygon (3–12 sides) with its interior and/or exterior angles marked by arcs and the angle sum derived. One figure for the interior-angle sum ((n − 2) × 180°, optionally shown by splitting into n − 2 triangles), regular-polygon angles (each interior = 180 − 360/n, each exterior = 360/n), the exterior-angle sum (360°) and forming/solving angle equations (an irregular polygon with one unknown interior angle). You give the polygon as a regular n-gon (the model generates it) or as an irregular vertex sketch (any units — only the shape matters); the model derives every angle measure, the sum, each regular angle, the triangle-split diagonals and the equal-side ticks. Mark every interior or exterior angle at once, or address one by its vertex number; occlude an angle or the sum ("find the missing angle"), highlight the answer, override a value as given data ("100°") or algebra ("2x"), and on the web drag a vertex to watch the interior sum stay (n − 2) × 180°.
whenToUse: Reach for this whenever the teaching is the angles of a polygon (a quadrilateral, pentagon, hexagon and up): the interior-angle sum, regular-polygon interior and exterior angles, exterior angles adding to 360°, and "form and solve an equation" for a missing interior angle. Choose the input: a regular polygon is regular: n (a regular n-gon is generated, sitting flat on its base) — use it for "the interior angles of a regular hexagon" or "an exterior angle of a regular octagon"; an irregular polygon is vertices: a list of [x, y] corners placed as a sketch in any units (the shape need not be to scale — set notToScale and override each given angle with a label). Common configurations: interior sum — showInteriorAngles to mark every interior angle, with angleSum { mode: "interior" } for the "(n − 2) × 180°" readout; add diagonalsFrom: 1 to fan the triangle-split that proves it. Regular angle — regular: n, showInteriorAngles (every angle the same), angleSum { perAngle: true } to show "÷ n = … each". Exterior angles — showExteriorAngles and angleSum { mode: "exterior" } (sum 360°, 360 ÷ n each). Find the missing angle — showInteriorAngles, then an angles entry on the unknown vertex with occlude: true, highlight: true, and angleSum showing the total so the pupil subtracts. Form an equation — give the sectors labels x, 2x via angles[].label and put the equation in the caption. Address one angle by its 1-based vertex number (at: 1 is the first vertex you listed, counting round the polygon); per-angle entries override the show-all flags so you can occlude or highlight just one. Occlude renders a value as "?"; the arc still shows. Set draggablePoints (irregular only) to let pupils reshape the polygon and watch the interior angles change while their sum stays (n − 2) × 180° — the invariant. Keep the same polygon across the blocks of one lesson so pupils track one figure; change only what is given, occluded or highlighted. Switch model when the teaching changes — for a triangle specifically (Pythagoras, trig, the 180° sum) use geometry/triangle; for parallel lines and a transversal use geometry/parallel-lines; for angles at a point, on a line, or vertically opposite use geometry/angles-at-a-point. Synonyms a teacher might use: polygon, interior angles, exterior angles, angle sum, sum of interior angles, sum of the angles, regular polygon, irregular polygon, pentagon, hexagon, heptagon, octagon, quadrilateral, missing angle, (n − 2) × 180, 360 degrees, each angle, form an equation, angle facts.

interface.description: Supply the polygon EXACTLY one way — regular (a generated regular n-gon) OR vertices (an irregular sketch) — then annotate. Every other property applies to both.

regular.description: Draw a REGULAR polygon with this many sides; the model generates the vertices (equal sides and angles), sitting flat on its base. Use 4 for a square, 5 a regular pentagon, 6 a regular hexagon, 8 an octagon, and so on. Give EITHER regular OR vertices, never both. Vertices are numbered 1 upward going anticlockwise from the lower-left corner.

vertices.description: Draw an IRREGULAR polygon from these corners, in order around the outline. Each corner is an [x, y] point in your OWN units (y up) — place them as a SKETCH; only the shape matters and the figure is auto-fitted to the canvas. The order numbers the vertices (the first is vertex 1) and is the direction angles are read round. Give EITHER vertices OR regular, never both. For a not-to-scale exam figure, set notToScale and override each given angle with a label.

items.description: One corner as [x, y] in your own units (y up).

angles.description: Per-vertex angle marks — list a vertex here only to occlude it, highlight it, override its value, or mark its exterior angle. The measure is DERIVED from the shape; an entry here OVERRIDES the showInteriorAngles / showExteriorAngles flags for that one vertex. Omit for none (or rely on the show-all flags).

at.description: Which vertex this angle sits at — its 1-based number (vertex 1 is the first you listed, or the start vertex of a regular polygon; counting round the outline). Must be a vertex the polygon has.

label.description: Override the displayed value — a given measure on a not-to-scale figure ("100°"), or algebra when forming an equation ("2x", "x + 20"). Omit to show the measure derived from the shape (e.g. "108°").

occlude.description: Render this angle's value as "?" — the "find the missing angle" hook. The arc still shows. Default false.

highlight.description: Draw the eye to this angle (amber arc + value) — the answer, or the angle a question is about. Default false.

exterior.description: Mark the EXTERIOR angle at this vertex (between the previous side extended past the vertex and the next side) instead of the interior one — the "turn" you make walking round the polygon, equal to 180 − interior. Intended for convex vertices. Default false (interior).

showInteriorAngles.description: Mark EVERY interior angle with an arc and its derived measure (a regular n-gon shows the same value at each vertex; a right angle shows as a small square). Per-vertex angles[] entries override individual vertices (e.g. to occlude the unknown one). Default false.

showExteriorAngles.description: Mark EVERY exterior angle (each side extended past its vertex, the turn arc and its derived measure). Pairs with angleSum mode "exterior" (they add to 360°). Best on a convex polygon. Default false.

angleSum.description: Include this to render the derived angle-sum readout below the figure; omit it for no readout. Both the working and the total are computed — you never type the sum, so it cannot be wrong.

mode.description: "interior" (default): "Sum of interior angles = (n − 2) × 180° = …". "exterior": "Sum of exterior angles = 360°".

showWorking.description: Show the working chain ("(6 − 2) × 180°") before the total. false shows just "= 720°". Default true.

perAngle.description: For a REGULAR polygon, also show the division to one angle — interior "… ÷ n = 120° each", exterior "360 ÷ n = 45°". Ignored for an irregular polygon (the angles differ). Default false.

occlude.description: Render the final total as "?" ("= ?") — "what is the sum?". The working, if shown, stays visible. Default false.

highlight.description: Amber the total — answer emphasis. Default false.

diagonalsFrom.description: Fan dashed construction diagonals from this vertex (its 1-based number) to every non-adjacent vertex, splitting the polygon into n − 2 triangles — the visual proof that the interior angles sum to (n − 2) × 180°. Omit for no diagonals.

showEqualMarks.description: Tick equal sides — a regular polygon gets one tick on every side (all equal); an irregular polygon ticks sides that share a length with matching tick counts. Signals "regular" / which sides are equal. Default false.

vertexLabels.description: Print a letter (A, B, C, …) just outside each vertex, going round the outline. Useful for an exam figure that names its corners. Default false.

notToScale.description: Print a "Not to scale" note by the figure. Only when the source figure prints one — most exam figures don't. Default false.

caption.description: An optional line centred below the figure: the rule, e.g. "The interior angles of a pentagon add to 540°". Omit for none. Never the question or an instruction: that wording is the block's text.

header.description: Optional short title centred above the figure; the top padding grows to clear it.

draggablePoints.description: Web-only, IRREGULAR polygons only. Let pupils drag a vertex to reshape the polygon; the interior and exterior angle measures recompute live while the interior sum stays (n − 2) × 180° — the invariant. Default false.
